status: Proposed mapping (Tab 27 Gate 0.2), R05 P3, extended with the P4a control fields. build-question-library.mjs turns this into ANSWER_CONFIG in src/lib/registerQuestions.js. Question wording is verbatim from Tab 21. Child options beyond the source wording are proposals for Blue Leaf to confirm in P4. P4b added the whole-house standards, zone-driven defaults, surface finishes and linked gutters. Option ids are stable from P4a: tab21-option-ids-v1.0.lock.json holds them, and a test fails if one goes.

mapping.fact_prefill: Read from Sales or the project. Never re-asked.
mapping.progressive_branch: Choose, then only the choices that follow from it. May stop at any level.
mapping.repeatable_scope: One item per element or area.
mapping.requirement: A required outcome, not a product.
mapping.action_risk: A follow-up or a risk, with an owner.
mapping.technical_only: Designer, consultant or trade check. Not a client question.

nature.fact: A fact about the site or household. Never construction scope.
nature.choice: A client product or finish choice.
nature.scope: Work Blue Leaf does or does not do.

tier.more_detail: Behind + More detail or Explore more.
tier.office_only: Office Register only. Not shown in a client meeting.

disposition.none: The generic work disposition is not a valid answer to this question.
disposition.element: Each repeated element carries its own disposition.
disposition.answer: The chosen option is the disposition.
disposition.settled_only: Disposition is only used to settle an item out: excluded, by others, deferred, N/A or retained.

optionSource.existing: The value already stored by the Hub.
optionSource.proposed: Not in the source documents. For Blue Leaf to confirm in P4.

select.groups: The top level is headings, each with its own choices.

presentationGroups.why: Tab 27 B06 and Gate 0.2: one area-linked path. Source ids are kept on the items, so nothing merges at the data level.
Tab 27 B07: one scope-first path. W-003 keeps its own promptKey.
R-002 is the disposition of R-003 today (render disposition_of:R-003).

questions.text: Project identity and address. Prompt to staff only if missing: Are we working on the correct client and site? Show current Sales value.
questions.group: ENTRY: PROJECT CONTEXT (MOSTLY PREFILLED FROM SALES)

questions.text: Drawings. Which plan set, sheet list, issue date and revision are we reviewing? Link existing document record; no reupload if present.
questions.group: ENTRY: PROJECT CONTEXT (MOSTLY PREFILLED FROM SALES)

questions.text: Concept Meeting/Presentation record and key decisions already made. Surface existing meeting facts; never force re-entry.
questions.group: ENTRY: PROJECT CONTEXT (MOSTLY PREFILLED FROM SALES)

questions.text: Client budget target, timing expectations and design priorities. Show current dated Sales fact; ask only to confirm material changes.
questions.group: ENTRY: PROJECT CONTEXT (MOSTLY PREFILLED FROM SALES)

questions.text: What do you most want to improve: space, natural light, comfort, privacy, entertaining, storage, accessibility, low maintenance, energy use? Pick up to 3 priorities plus note.
questions.group: ENTRY: PROJECT CONTEXT (MOSTLY PREFILLED FROM SALES)
questions.notes: Existing records hold a comma string in description: read as legacy text, never parsed. The note is written for the client and printed in the Client Brief, so it is answer.clientNote and never the staff-only note.

questions.text: What parts of the property are in this project, what are possible extras, and what is explicitly future work? Tag areas as Included / Optional / Excluded / Deferred.
questions.group: ENTRY: PROJECT CONTEXT (MOSTLY PREFILLED FROM SALES)
questions.notes: Keeps the existing one-item-per-area pattern from ContextStep.

questions.text: Physical project type: New Build / Renovation / Extension / Combined. Delivery model separately Design & Build / Build Only / Management / Other; never combine types in one ambiguous field.
questions.group: ENTRY: PROJECT CONTEXT (MOSTLY PREFILLED FROM SALES)
questions.notes: Delivery model and physical type stay two separate facts.

questions.text: Will the property remain occupied or operational through work? Record temporary facility and access requirements only when relevant.
questions.group: ENTRY: PROJECT CONTEXT (MOSTLY PREFILLED FROM SALES)
questions.notes: Option ids equal the stored meta.occupancy values.

questions.text: Which decisions must be made before the next architect issue, budget check or PTSA? Owner, not necessarily due date.
questions.group: ENTRY: PROJECT CONTEXT (MOSTLY PREFILLED FROM SALES)
questions.notes: One action per decision, with an owner. Due date optional.

questions.text: Existing architects/consultants/suppliers and known agreements; link from Hub, not new text if authoritative contact already exists.
questions.group: ENTRY: PROJECT CONTEXT (MOSTLY PREFILLED FROM SALES)

questions.text: Site access: restricted driveway, narrow site, crane/delivery access, neighbour restrictions, steep slope or parking? Note known facts, inspection tasks.
questions.notes: A recorded constraint is a fact. Never construction Included. Scope only if a physical access change is explicitly added as its own item.

questions.text: Survey, boundaries, easements, services, geotech and site levels: which reports exist and which are required? Internal consultant action, not client specification.
questions.notes: Internal consultant action, not a client specification.

questions.text: Trees, retaining walls, external structures and landscaping affected by construction? Include/retain/protect/remove/by others.
What is being demolished, retained, altered and made good in the existing building? Record by area, not one vague demolition line.
questions.notes: One path for W-004, W-006 and W-008. No meeting-stage measurement. Each entry is its own item with its own id.

questions.text: Existing structural, moisture, termite, asbestos/contamination, roof and foundation conditions: inspected / assumed / needs test; source.
questions.notes: Risk and investigation with an owner and source. Inspected, Assumed and Needs test are statements about the condition above them, so they never carry across to a different condition.

questions.text: What existing finishes and fixtures must be protected and/or matched? Note acceptable variation or inability to match exact old products.
questions.notes: Reached through the Protect and Match actions on the W-004 path. Items keep promptKey W-006, so the source id survives.

questions.text: Will the family live on site? Work zones, temporary kitchen/bathroom, dust separation, service outages and safe access.
questions.notes: A client answer is never New or Remove. Yes opens the branch.

questions.text: Where do new and existing work connect: roof, wall, floor, drainage, electrical, thermal envelope? Add interface action and drawing ref.
questions.notes: Optional driver on the W-004 path. Records an interface action and a drawing reference, not a demolition measurement.

questions.text: Overall project quality priorities: standard / upgraded / individually specified, and where is investment most important? Do not fabricate a universal inclusions package.
questions.notes: The client's own quality priority. Not the Blue Leaf baseline pricing tier (P4b), which is a separate labelled assumption and is never read from this answer.

questions.text: External works scope: driveway, landscaping, paths, fencing, retaining, pergola, pool or boundary work included/excluded/deferred?
questions.notes: Construction type and finish are asked only for New, Replace and Alter. No material burden for retained or excluded elements. No quantities. The construction-type lists are proposed for Blue Leaf to confirm.

questions.text: Unknown conditions likely to affect cost and design. Is investigation, contingency, exclusion or alternate scope appropriate?
questions.notes: Risk item with description, source, responsible party, status and next action. Never a generic disposition.

questions.text: Planning/building approval and consultant design responsibilities. Identify who verifies requirements, not legal assertions based on questionnaire.
questions.notes: Identifies who verifies. Makes no legal assertion.

questions.text: Overall architectural material direction: masonry, render, lightweight cladding, timber feature, metal roof? What should the home look and feel like?
questions.group: WHOLE-HOUSE GENERAL INCLUSIONS AND MATERIAL STANDARDS
questions.notes: Each system is its own item with zone and status (DEC-MRUX-01). 'Metal roof' in the Tab 21 wording is captured under W-014. Technical suitability stays a review action.

questions.text: Roof and gutter colour/material preference; roof profile/pitch/box gutter details to architect later.
questions.group: WHOLE-HOUSE GENERAL INCLUSIONS AND MATERIAL STANDARDS
questions.notes: One row per roof system, told apart by zone, so a pitched main roof and a low-pitch alfresco are separate records. Gutters are a separate linked item under each roof, not hidden in the roof colour. Pitch and profile compatibility verified against plans and manufacturer data. Colour tones are proposed for Blue Leaf to confirm.

questions.text: Windows and glazing priorities: frame appearance, opening use, sun/shading, privacy, thermal/acoustic performance, insect screens.
questions.group: WHOLE-HOUSE GENERAL INCLUSIONS AND MATERIAL STANDARDS
questions.notes: A preference claims no compliance with energy, acoustic, bushfire or consent requirements.

questions.text: Envelope quality: comfort/energy efficiency, insulation, airtightness and moisture management priority. Technical compliance by designers.
questions.group: WHOLE-HOUSE GENERAL INCLUSIONS AND MATERIAL STANDARDS
questions.notes: Independent goals, not certification decisions. The card lists staff-only suggestions, marked review required, derived from the goals chosen and never stored (DEC-MRUX-03). No product is specified by selecting a goal.

questions.text: General interior floor palette by zone: timber/laminate/hybrid/tile/carpet/polished concrete, wet-area separate.
questions.group: WHOLE-HOUSE GENERAL INCLUSIONS AND MATERIAL STANDARDS
questions.notes: One default item per zone, shown as one row each. Rooms inherit by zone, from roomZones. A room with no default for its zone asks the question. Exceptions are explicit.

questions.text: Internal doors and trims: standard or feature doors, general door heights, skirting/architraves/cornice and hardware style.
questions.group: WHOLE-HOUSE GENERAL INCLUSIONS AND MATERIAL STANDARDS
questions.notes: One record, with each group its own default (MR-UX-01F). Door height, jamb and hardware first; the rest behind + More detail. Fire, acoustic and door-height exceptions are recorded per room on R-007.

questions.text: General paint and ceiling finish direction: warm/cool palette, matte/sheen, square set/cornice, feature areas.
questions.group: WHOLE-HOUSE GENERAL INCLUSIONS AND MATERIAL STANDARDS
questions.notes: One row per surface. No generic sheen chip: a finish level is only offered under a surface, behind + More detail, and each surface shows its usual level until someone chooses. Usual levels are proposed for Blue Leaf to confirm.

questions.text: Heating/cooling, ventilation and hot water preference; any required comfort zones or special rooms?
questions.group: WHOLE-HOUSE GENERAL INCLUSIONS AND MATERIAL STANDARDS
questions.notes: Preference only. Sizing and design by the trade.

questions.text: Electrical, smart home, data, solar/battery/EV charging ambitions; note special requirements, not layouts yet.
questions.group: WHOLE-HOUSE GENERAL INCLUSIONS AND MATERIAL STANDARDS

questions.text: Window furnishings, appliances, loose furniture, fireplaces, landscaping, security and automation: included, by client, excluded or future?
questions.group: WHOLE-HOUSE GENERAL INCLUSIONS AND MATERIAL STANDARDS
questions.notes: Separate line per element with + Add another (MR-UX-01H). Never one sentence. By client records who supplies. Whether that puts it outside the contract is Tab 27 Q4, still open, so it sets no disposition yet.

questions.text: Standard supply/installation responsibilities for selected products and any client-supplied items; warranty and lead time implications noted internally.
questions.group: WHOLE-HOUSE GENERAL INCLUSIONS AND MATERIAL STANDARDS
questions.notes: Who supplies and who installs is open policy (Tab 27 Q4). Uses the existing supplyBy field until decided.

questions.text: Document current building performance goal and required consultant checks (energy, thermal, fire, acoustic, moisture, accessibility as applicable). No automatic certification label.
questions.group: WHOLE-HOUSE GENERAL INCLUSIONS AND MATERIAL STANDARDS
questions.notes: No automatic certification label.

questions.text: Identify outstanding whole-house decision that materially changes cost/design and allocate owner.
questions.group: WHOLE-HOUSE GENERAL INCLUSIONS AND MATERIAL STANDARDS

questions.text: Room/zone name, level, drawing sheet/revision, order on plans; type: kitchen, bathroom, bedroom, hall, external etc.

questions.notes: R-002 supplies the options, with an optional short note. Superseded by a room-specific scope prompt where one leads (partitionRoomPrompts).

questions.notes: Tree comes from W-019.

questions.text: Internal/external doors, windows, screens or opening alterations specific to this room.
